method: Two-level thesaurus built on ISO 25964, ANSI/NISO Z39.19 and SKOS practice: one preferred label, altLabels as non-preferred terms, up to two parents with the first as primary.

Literary warrant: every term is backed by a live faceted tag, a raw image subject, a #4856 browse topic, a live collection, or a Kanripo class in the sibu catalogue. A script checked each warrant string against the data.
Warrant prefixes: tag: faceted tag, image: raw metadata.subjects string, topic: #4856 browse topic, collection: collection slug, sibu: Kanripo class.
A first draft of 376 terms was cut to 250 by folding thinner terms into a broader one. Their labels became altLabels and their tags became merges.
FAST ids come only from the fastsuggest API. Wikidata ids come only from wbsearchentities, each read against its description. A script confirmed every stored id appears in a saved API response.
Match is exact when the heading or item means the same as the term, close when it is a neighbouring or broader idea.
Labels in la, es, nl, de and zh are Wikidata labels of items matched exactly, plus a few hand-entered Chinese titles. Close matches give no translations, so nothing is guessed.
imageCount is the largest single total from /api/gallery?limit=1 with subject= or topic=, default quality threshold 0.7. Totals are never added together.

bookCount is the largest single figure from /api/books/facets, a collection's total_book_count, or a sum of disjoint sibu classes. Sibu figures count works in the repo snapshot of 2026-11-04, not volumes.
An extra field, countSource, says which query gave each count. It was not in the requested shape.
notes: No cataloguer or subject specialist has reviewed this. Treat it as a draft for that review.
Counts are floors, not totals. Only about 30% of books are tagged, and books and images are counted by different routes, so counts are not comparable between terms.

sourcelibrary.org was rate limiting during this work, so calls were cut to one every 3.3 seconds, obeying Retry-After. All planned image queries finished, but the plan shrank: only the raw strings used here were counted, not all 2,144.
34 terms have a null imageCount because no raw subject or topic maps to them. That does not mean they have no images.

The facets route returned HTTP 500 for 11 of 12 cross-facet intersections, and these were not retried. Merged terms such as alchemy, kabbalah and hermeticism therefore show the larger single figure, not the true union.

/api/search was not used, as it failed during rate limiting. So topics with no tag, image subject or collection were never tested, including plague (the example in the plan), Talmud, Spiritualism and Inca. They may deserve terms.
Warrant rests on tag, subject and collection names. Book contents were not read. Provenance collections used as evidence, such as bhutan for Tibetan Buddhism, are an assumption.
Raw image strings outside src/data/image-subject-map.json were not seen.
The tags classical (8,433) and christian-mystical (5,380) look over-applied. They are merged but not used for counts.

Weak areas: Judaism has few terms, as the corpus evidence found was thin. Korean has no term. Indonesian material is the weakest placement: balinese-art sits under Indian religions and javanese-culture under Society and Literature, both for want of a better home.
Balinese Narrative Drawings shows bookCount 1 and a null imageCount, but its collection record lists 304 artworks.

Left out as too thin: Sikhism, Druze, Baha'i, Mandaeanism, Samaritans (gallery sets of 4 images or fewer), Australian Aboriginal traditions (1 book), and single Native American nations, which are altLabels of one term.
People are left out as subjects, for example Leonardo da Vinci and Paracelsus. They need a decision: names may suit a separate list.
Many Chinese terms combine a place and a topic. Some could become a topic plus a language filter once the filters exist.
Top-level labels with 'and' are navigation headings, which Z39.19 would treat as compound. Religions are top-level siblings of Religion and mysticism only because the list stops at two levels.

FAST: Mathematics has null because the suggest API did not surface the plain heading, though it very likely exists. Aristotelianism, Paracelsianism and several place-plus-topic terms have no fitting heading in the results.
Non-English labels come from Wikidata unreviewed and vary in quality, Latin most of all. Coverage is uneven.
Form, sphere, era and mode tag values were left out as filters, apart from topic-like ones such as scripture and encyclopedia.
Confidence is a drafting judgement about the term and its placement, not a measured score. High is the default where nothing raised doubt, so it is generous.

subjects.label: Religion and mysticism
subjects.scopeNote: Ideas and practices shared across religions. Works on one tradition go under that tradition.

subjects.label: Indian religions
subjects.scopeNote: Religions that began in India, apart from Buddhism, which has its own heading.

subjects.label: East Asian religion and thought
subjects.scopeNote: Confucian, Daoist, Shinto and related traditions of China, Japan and Korea, and the knowledge systems classed with them. Buddhism has its own heading.

subjects.label: Indigenous traditions
subjects.scopeNote: Knowledge, religion and history of Indigenous peoples of the Americas, Africa and the Pacific. Much of this material was written down by outsiders.

subjects.label: Esoteric traditions
subjects.scopeNote: Western currents of hidden or initiatory knowledge. Alchemy, magic and astrology have their own headings.

subjects.label: Arts
subjects.scopeNote: Visual arts, architecture and music as subjects. Literature has its own heading.

subjects.label: Natural philosophy
subjects.scopeNote: Early enquiry into nature as a whole, before it divided into the separate sciences.
